sanskrit: sāpanīya tam āyāsam upaspṛśya jalaṃ śuci cakāra mātā rāmasya maṅgalāni manasvinī
english: Having performed her ablutions and touched the pure water, putting aside that distress, Rāma's wise and noble mother performed the auspicious rites.

sanskrit: svasti sādhyāś ca viśve ca marutaś ca maharṣayaḥ svasti dhātā vidhātā ca svasti pūṣā bhago 'ryamā
english: May the Sādhyas, the Viśvas, the Maruts, and the great seers bestow well-being; may Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, Pūṣan, Bhaga, and Aryaman bestow well-being.

sanskrit: ṛtavaś caiva pakṣāś ca māsāḥ saṃvatsarāḥ kṣapāḥ dināni ca muhūrtāś ca svasti kurvantu te sadā
english: May the seasons, the fortnights, the months, the years, the nights, the days, and the hours always bring you well-being.

sanskrit: smṛtir dhṛtiś ca dharmaś ca pāntu tvāṃ putra sarvataḥ skandaś ca bhagavān devaḥ somaś ca sabṛhaspatiḥ
english: May Memory, Fortitude, and Dharma protect you on all sides, my son; and may the divine lord Skanda, Soma, and Bṛhaspati protect you.

sanskrit: saptarṣayo nāradaś ca te tvāṃ rakṣantu sarvataḥ nakṣatrāṇi ca sarvāṇi grahāś ca sahadevatāḥ mahāvanāni carato muniveṣasya dhīmataḥ
english: May the Seven Seers and Nārada protect you on all sides; may all the lunar mansions and the planets together with their presiding deities protect you, the wise one clad in an ascetic's garb as you roam the great forests.

sanskrit: plavagā vṛścikā daṃśā maśakāś caiva kānane sarīsṛpāś ca kīṭāś ca mā bhūvan gahane tava
english: May jumping creatures, scorpions, biting insects, mosquitoes, reptiles, and all manner of bugs in the dense forest cause you no harm.

sanskrit: mahādvipāś ca siṃhāś ca vyāghrā ṛkṣāś ca daṃṣṭriṇaḥ mahiṣāḥ śṛṅgiṇo raudrā na te druhyantu putraka
english: May the great elephants, lions, tigers, bears with their fangs, and the fierce horned buffalo do you no harm, my dear son.

sanskrit: nṛmāṃsabhojanā raudrā ye cānye sattvajātayaḥ mā ca tvāṃ hiṃsiṣuḥ putra mayā saṃpūjitās tv iha
english: May the terrible beings who feed on human flesh, and whatever other kinds of creatures there may be, do you no injury, my son — for I have duly propitiated them here.

sanskrit: āgamās te śivāḥ santu sidhyantu ca parākramāḥ sarvasaṃpattayo rāma svastimān gaccha putraka
english: May your journeys be auspicious; may your feats of valor be accomplished; may all prosperity attend you, Rāma. Go in safety, my son.

sanskrit: svasti te 'stv āntarikṣebhyaḥ pārthivebhyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ sarvebhyaś caiva devebhyo ye ca te paripanthinaḥ
english: May there be well-being for you again and again from the celestial regions and from the earthly regions; from all the gods, and from those who obstruct your path.

sanskrit: sarvalokaprabhur brahmā bhūtabhartā tatharṣayaḥ ye ca śeṣāḥ surās te tvāṃ rakṣantu vanavāsinam
english: May Brahmā, the lord of all worlds, the sustainer of all beings, along with the sages and the remaining gods, protect you as you dwell in the forest.

sanskrit: iti mālyaiḥ suragaṇān gandhaiś cāpi yaśasvinī stutibhiś cānurūpābhir ānarcāyatalocanā
english: With these words, that illustrious wide-eyed woman honored the hosts of gods with garlands, perfumes, and fitting hymns of praise.

sanskrit: yan maṅgalaṃ sahasrākṣe sarvadevanamaskṛte vṛtranāśe samabhavat tat te bhavatu maṅgalam
english: Whatever auspiciousness arose for the thousand-eyed Indra, saluted by all gods, at the slaying of Vṛtra — may that same auspiciousness be yours.

sanskrit: yan maṅgalaṃ suparṇasya vinatākalpayat purā amṛtaṃ prārthayānasya tat te bhavatu maṅgalam
english: Whatever auspiciousness Vinatā fashioned long ago for Suparṇa — Garuḍa — when he was seeking the nectar of immortality, may that auspiciousness be yours.

sanskrit: oṣadhīṃ cāpi siddhārthāṃ viśalyakaraṇīṃ śubhām cakāra rakṣāṃ kausalyā mantrair abhijajāpa ca
english: Kausalyā also fashioned a protective charm using the efficacious and auspicious herb Viśalyakaraṇī, and muttered the appropriate sacred formulas over it.

sanskrit: ānamya mūrdhni cāghrāya pariṣvajya yaśasvinī avadat putra siddhārtho gaccha rāma yathāsukham
english: Bowing, smelling his head, and embracing him, that illustrious woman said: "Go comfortably, Rāma, my son, your purposes fulfilled."

sanskrit: arogaṃ sarvasiddhārtham ayodhyāṃ punar āgatam paśyāmi tvāṃ sukhaṃ vatsa susthitaṃ rājaveśmani
english: "May I see you again, my dear child, returned to Ayodhyā healthy, all your aims accomplished, dwelling happily and well established in the royal palace."

sanskrit: mayārcitā devagaṇāḥ śivādayo maharṣayo bhūtamahāsuroragāḥ abhiprayātasya vanaṃ cirāya te hitāni kāṅkṣantu diśaś ca rāghava
english: "The bands of gods headed by Śiva, the great seers, the beings, great asuras, and serpents that I have honored — may they and all the directions long desire your welfare, O Rāghava, as you depart for the forest."

sanskrit: itīva cāśrupratipūrṇalocanā samāpya ca svastyayanaṃ yathāvidhi pradakṣiṇaṃ caiva cakāra rāghavaṃ punaḥ punaś cāpi nipīḍya sasvaje
english: Having spoken thus with eyes brimming with tears, and having duly completed the benedictory rites, she circumambulated the Rāghava and again and again pressed him tightly in her embrace.

sanskrit: tathā tu devyā sa kṛtapradakṣiṇo nipīḍya mātuś caraṇau punaḥ punaḥ jagāma sītānilayaṃ mahāyaśāḥ sa rāghavaḥ prajvalitaḥ svayā śriyā
english: Having thus been circumambulated by the queen, and having pressed his mother's feet again and again, that great-glorious Rāghava, blazing with his own splendor, departed for the dwelling of Sītā.

sanskrit: abhivādya tu kausalyāṃ rāmaḥ saṃprasthito vanam kṛtasvastyayano mātrā dharmiṣṭhe vartmani sthitaḥ
english: Having reverenced Kausalyā, Rāma set out for the forest, blessed with the auspicious rites performed by his mother, steadfast on the path of righteousness.

sanskrit: virājayan rājasuto rājamārgaṃ narair vṛtam hṛdayāny āmamantheva janasya guṇavattayā
english: The prince, illuminating the royal road crowded with people, seemed to churn the hearts of the assembled folk by the sheer power of his virtues.

sanskrit: vaidehī cāpi tat sarvaṃ na śuśrāva tapasvinī tad eva hṛdi tasyāś ca yauvarājyābhiṣecanam
english: The afflicted Vaidehī had heard none of all this, for in her heart there was only the expectation of Rāma's consecration as crown prince.

sanskrit: devakāryaṃ sma sā kṛtvā kṛtajñā hṛṣṭacetanā abhijñā rājadharmāṇāṃ rājaputraṃ pratīkṣate
english: Having performed her worship of the gods, that grateful and joyful woman, well versed in the duties of royalty, awaited the prince.

sanskrit: praviveśātha rāmas tu svaveśma suvibhūṣitam prahṛṣṭajanasaṃpūrṇaṃ hriyā kiṃ cid avāṅmukhaḥ
english: Then Rāma entered his own beautifully adorned dwelling, filled with joyful attendants, his face cast slightly downward out of shame.

sanskrit: atha sītā samutpatya vepamānā ca taṃ patim apaśyac chokasaṃtaptaṃ cintāvyākulitendriyam
english: Then Sītā sprang up and beheld her husband trembling — scorched by grief, his senses disturbed by anxious thoughts.

sanskrit: vivarṇavadanaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ prasvinnam amarṣaṇam āha duḥkhābhisaṃtaptā kim idānīm idaṃ prabho
english: Seeing his face pale and streaming with perspiration, beside himself with agitation, and herself scorched by grief, she said: "What is this now, my lord?"

sanskrit: adya bārhaspataḥ śrīmān yuktaḥ puṣyo na rāghava procyate brāhmaṇaiḥ prājñaiḥ kena tvam asi durmanāḥ
english: "Today, O Rāghava, the auspicious Puṣya asterism is in conjunction with Bṛhaspati — so declare the learned Brāhmaṇas. Why then are you downcast?"

sanskrit: na te śataśalākena jalaphenanibhena ca āvṛtaṃ vadanaṃ valgu chatreṇābhivirājate
english: "Your lovely face is not graced, as it should be, by the royal parasol with its hundred ribs, white as the foam of water, held above it."

sanskrit: vyajanābhyāṃ ca mukhyābhyāṃ śatapatranibhekṣaṇam candrahaṃsaprakāśābhyāṃ vījyate na tavānanam
english: "Your face, whose eyes resemble the lotus, is not being fanned by the two principal fly-whisks, white as the moon and the swan."

sanskrit: vāgmino bandinaś cāpi prahṛṣṭās tvaṃ nararṣabha stuvanto nādya dṛśyante maṅgalaiḥ sūtamāgadhāḥ
english: "O bull among men, the eloquent bards and panegyrists — the Sūtas and the Māgadhas — are not seen today joyfully singing your praises with auspicious hymns."

sanskrit: na te kṣaudraṃ ca dadhi ca brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ mūrdhni mūrdhāvasiktasya dadhati sma vidhānataḥ
english: "The Brāhmaṇas who are masters of the Veda are not placing honey and curds upon your head in the prescribed manner, as upon one who has had the consecration poured over him."

sanskrit: na tvāṃ prakṛtayaḥ sarvā śreṇīmukhyāś ca bhūṣitāḥ anuvrajitum icchanti paurajānapadās tathā
english: "All the ministers of state, adorned with ornaments, and the heads of the guilds, together with the townspeople and the country folk, do not seem to wish to accompany you."

sanskrit: caturbhir vegasaṃpannair hayaiḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ mukhyaḥ puṣyaratho yuktaḥ kiṃ na gacchati te 'grataḥ
english: "Why does the chief ceremonial chariot, yoked to four swift horses adorned with golden ornaments, not go before you?"

sanskrit: na hastī cāgrataḥ śrīmāṃs tava lakṣaṇapūjitaḥ prayāṇe lakṣyate vīra kṛṣṇameghagiri prabhaḥ
english: "Nor is the auspicious, mark-honored elephant, dark as a rain cloud or a mountain, seen going before you in the procession, O hero."

sanskrit: na ca kāñcanacitraṃ te paśyāmi priyadarśana bhadrāsanaṃ puraskṛtya yāntaṃ vīrapuraḥsaram
english: "Nor do I see the golden, ornately decorated throne being carried ahead of you, O fair to behold, with heroes marching before it."

sanskrit: abhiṣeko yadā sajjaḥ kim idānīm idaṃ tava apūrvo mukhavarṇaś ca na praharṣaś ca lakṣyate
english: "When the consecration was ready, what has now happened to you? Your complexion is unprecedented, and no exhilaration is visible in you."

sanskrit: itīva vilapantīṃ tāṃ provāca raghunandanaḥ sīte tatrabhavāṃs tāta pravrājayati māṃ vanam
english: To her lamenting thus, the delight of the Raghu clan spoke: "Sītā, the revered lord — my father — is sending me into exile in the forest."

sanskrit: kule mahati saṃbhūte dharmajñe dharmacāriṇi śṛṇu jānaki yenedaṃ krameṇābhyāgataṃ mama
english: "O Jānakī, born of a great lineage, one who knows righteousness and walks in its ways, listen to how this has come about step by step."

sanskrit: rājñā satyapratijñena pitrā daśarathena me kaikeyyai prītamanasā purā dattau mahāvarau
english: "My father King Daśaratha, a man of true vows, once gladly granted two great boons to Kaikeyī."

sanskrit: tayādya mama sajje 'sminn abhiṣeke nṛpodyate pracoditaḥ sa samayo dharmeṇa pratinirjitaḥ
english: "Now, today, when the king had made ready my consecration, she has called in that old debt; that appointed time has been invoked and compelled by dharma."

sanskrit: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi vastavyaṃ daṇḍake mayā pitrā me bharataś cāpi yauvarājye niyojitaḥ so 'haṃ tvām āgato draṣṭuṃ prasthito vijanaṃ vanam
english: "I must dwell in the Daṇḍaka forest for fourteen years; my father has also installed Bharata as crown prince. I have come to see you before I depart for the uninhabited forest."

sanskrit: bharatasya samīpe te nāhaṃ kathyaḥ kadā cana ṛddhiyuktā hi puruṣā na sahante parastavam tasmān na te guṇāḥ kathyā bharatasyāgrato mama
english: "You should never speak of me in Bharata's presence. Men who have attained power cannot endure praise of a rival; therefore my virtues should not be spoken of before Bharata."

sanskrit: nāpi tvaṃ tena bhartavyā viśeṣeṇa kadā cana anukūlatayā śakyaṃ samīpe tasya vartitum
english: "Nor should you ever be treated by him as a special charge; you can comport yourself near him only with compliance and agreeableness."

sanskrit: ahaṃ cāpi pratijñāṃ tāṃ guroḥ samanupālayan vanam adyaiva yāsyāmi sthirā bhava manasvini
english: "I too, honoring that promise made to my elder, shall depart for the forest this very day. Be steadfast, O wise one."

sanskrit: yāte ca mayi kalyāṇi vanaṃ muniniṣevitam vratopavāsaratayā bhavitavyaṃ tvayānaghe
english: "And when I have gone to the forest frequented by sages, O auspicious one, O sinless one, you must be devoted to vows and fasts."

sanskrit: kālyam utthāya devānāṃ kṛtvā pūjāṃ yathāvidhi vanditavyo daśarathaḥ pitā mama nareśvaraḥ
english: "Rising early in the morning and performing the worship of the gods in the prescribed manner, you must pay reverence to Daśaratha, my father, the lord of men."

sanskrit: mātā ca mama kausalyā vṛddhā saṃtāpakarśitā dharmam evāgrataḥ kṛtvā tvattaḥ saṃmānam arhati
english: "And my mother Kausalyā, aged and worn thin by grief, deserves your respect, placing dharma above all else."

sanskrit: vanditavyāś ca te nityaṃ yāḥ śeṣā mama mātaraḥ snehapraṇayasaṃbhogaiḥ samā hi mama mātaraḥ
english: "You must always revere my other mothers as well, for in terms of affection, tenderness, and the enjoyment of my company, they are all equal to my mother."

sanskrit: bhrātṛputrasamau cāpi draṣṭavyau ca viśeṣataḥ tvayā lakṣmaṇaśatrughnau prāṇaiḥ priyatarau mama
english: "And Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna, who are dearer to me than my own life, are to be regarded by you especially as sons and brothers alike."

sanskrit: vipriyaṃ na ca kartavyaṃ bharatasya kadā cana sa hi rājā prabhuś caiva deśasya ca kulasya ca
english: "And you must never do anything disagreeable to Bharata, for he is now the king and lord both of the realm and of the family."

sanskrit: ārādhitā hi śīlena prayatnaiś copasevitāḥ rājānaḥ saṃprasīdanti prakupyanti viparyaye
english: "Kings who are gratified by good conduct and attended upon with effort become gracious; in the contrary case they grow wrathful."

sanskrit: aurasān api putrān hi tyajanty ahitakāriṇaḥ samarthān saṃpragṛhṇanti janān api narādhipāḥ
english: "Kings abandon even their own natural sons if they act against their interests, and embrace even ordinary people who serve them capably."

sanskrit: ahaṃ gamiṣyāmi mahāvanaṃ priye tvayā hi vastavyam ihaiva bhāmini yathā vyalīkaṃ kuruṣe na kasya cit tathā tvayā kāryam idaṃ vaco mama
english: "I shall depart for the great forest, my dear; you must remain here, O beautiful one. So that you do no wrong to anyone, act in accordance with these words of mine."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu vaidehī priyārhā priyavādinī praṇayād eva saṃkruddhā bhartāram idam abravīt
english: Thus addressed, Vaidehī — who deserved only tender words and spoke only tender words — became indignant out of deep love, and spoke these words to her husband.

sanskrit: āryaputra pitā mātā bhrātā putras tathā snuṣā svāni puṇyāni bhuñjānāḥ svaṃ svaṃ bhāgyam upāsate
english: "O noble son, a father, a mother, a brother, a son — and likewise a daughter-in-law — each enjoys the fruits of their own merit and tends to their own separate destiny."

sanskrit: bhartur bhāgyaṃ tu bhāryaikā prāpnoti puruṣarṣabha ataś caivāham ādiṣṭā vane vastavyam ity api
english: "But a wife, O bull among men, partakes solely of her husband's fortune. Thus it is I who have been destined to dwell in the forest as well."

sanskrit: na pitā nātmajo nātmā na mātā na sakhījanaḥ iha pretya ca nārīṇāṃ patir eko gatiḥ sadā
english: "Neither a father, nor a son, nor one's own self, nor a mother, nor a circle of friends — in this world and after death, the husband is ever the sole refuge of women."

sanskrit: yadi tvaṃ prasthito durgaṃ vanam adyaiva rāghava agratas te gamiṣyāmi mṛdnantī kuśakaṇṭakān
english: "If you depart today for that inaccessible forest, O Rāghava, I shall go before you, crushing underfoot the sharp kuśa grass and thorns."

sanskrit: īrṣyā roṣau bahiṣkṛtya bhuktaśeṣam ivodakam naya māṃ vīra viśrabdhaḥ pāpaṃ mayi na vidyate
english: "Setting aside jealousy and anger as one sets aside water left over after a meal, take me with you without apprehension, O hero — no sin resides in me."

sanskrit: prāsādāgrair vimānair vā vaihāyasagatena vā sarvāvasthāgatā bhartuḥ pādacchāyā viśiṣyate
english: "Whatever the condition — whether in palace towers, or aerial mansions, or traveling through the sky — the shadow of a husband's feet excels them all."

sanskrit: anuśiṣṭāsmi mātrā ca pitrā ca vividhāśrayam nāsmi saṃprati vaktavyā vartitavyaṃ yathā mayā
english: "I have been instructed by my mother and my father in conduct befitting all manner of circumstances; I need not now be told how I should comport myself."

sanskrit: sukhaṃ vane nivatsyāmi yathaiva bhavane pituḥ acintayantī trīṃl lokāṃś cintayantī pativratam
english: "I shall dwell happily in the forest just as in my father's house, giving no thought to the three worlds, but thinking only of my vow to my husband."

sanskrit: śuśrūṣamāṇā te nityaṃ niyatā brahmacāriṇī saha raṃsye tvayā vīra vaneṣu madhugandhiṣu
english: "Ever attending upon you, self-disciplined, and observing the vow of chastity, I shall take delight with you, O hero, in the honey-fragrant forests."

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi kartuṃ vane śakto rāma saṃparipālanam anyasya pai janasyeha kiṃ punar mama mānada
english: "For you, Rāma, are able to protect in the forest the people of others — how much more so me, O giver of honor."

sanskrit: phalamūlāśanā nityaṃ bhaviṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ na te duḥkhaṃ kariṣyāmi nivasantī saha tvayā
english: "I shall subsist always on fruits and roots, without doubt. Living with you, I shall cause you no hardship."

sanskrit: icchāmi saritaḥ śailān palvalāni vanāni ca draṣṭuṃ sarvatra nirbhītā tvayā nāthena dhīmatā
english: "I long to see the rivers, the mountains, the lakes, and the forests everywhere, fearless in every place, with you, my wise lord, as my protector."

sanskrit: haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇāḥ padminīḥ sādhupuṣpitāḥ iccheyaṃ sukhinī draṣṭuṃ tvayā vīreṇa saṃgatā
english: "I would wish, made happy by union with you, O hero, to behold the lotus pools thronged with geese and kāraṇḍava ducks, their lotuses in full and beautiful bloom."

sanskrit: saha tvayā viśālākṣa raṃsye paramanandinī evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇāṃ śataṃ vāhaṃ tvayā saha
english: "With you, O large-eyed one, I shall take the greatest delight — and thus I could dwell with you for a hundred thousand years."

sanskrit: svarge 'pi ca vinā vāso bhavitā yadi rāghava tvayā mama naravyāghra nāhaṃ tam api rocaye
english: "And if my abode, O Rāghava, O tiger among men, were to be even in heaven but without you, I should not desire that either."

sanskrit: ahaṃ gamiṣyāmi vanaṃ sudurgamaṃ mṛgāyutaṃ vānaravāraṇair yutam vane nivatsyāmi yathā pitur gṛhe tavaiva pādāv upagṛhya saṃmatā
english: "I shall go to the forest most difficult to traverse, filled with deer, inhabited by monkeys and elephants; I shall dwell in the forest as in my father's house, clasping your very feet, honored by you."

sanskrit: ananyabhāvām anuraktacetasaṃ tvayā viyuktāṃ maraṇāya niścitām nayasva māṃ sādhu kuruṣva yācanāṃ na te mayāto gurutā bhaviṣyati
english: "Take me — whose mind is set on none other, whose heart cleaves to you alone, who am resolved on death if separated from you. Do this kindness, grant my entreaty; no burden shall thereby fall upon you from me."

sanskrit: tathā bruvāṇām api dharmavatsalo na ca sma sītāṃ nṛvaro ninīṣati uvāca caināṃ bahu saṃnivartane vane nivāsasya ca duḥkhitāṃ prati
english: Yet even as she spoke thus, that best of men, attached to righteousness, did not intend to take Sītā; and he spoke to her at length, on the subject of dissuasion, and concerning the hardships of dwelling in the forest, addressing her in her distress.
